title: Vampire Planet: Hey DiCaprio, Bezos Ain’t Our Friend
author: Joshua Frank
content:
[![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/08/IMG_2298-680x450.jpeg)](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/08/14/vampire-
planet-hey-dicaprio-bezos-aint-our-friend/)

![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/08/IMG_2298-680x450.jpeg)

Amazon AWS data center, image Wikipedia.

Most would agree that the animals suffering as the world burns need our help.
So Jeff Bezos and Leonardo DiCaprio's $200 million commitment to the Phoenix
Species Project to revive 100 endangered species around the world should be
welcome news.

Leo believes it is.

"I could not be prouder to announce this," DiCaprio wrote joyously in an
Instagram post. "Save these species, and we protect everything around them.
The forests, the rivers, and the climate itself."

I sincerely hope that’s true and that these creatures,
[including](https://apnews.com/article/leonardo-dicaprio-jeff-bezos-
endangered-species-project-32320ba8dd021f162021d08050aaa9d3) a lemur in
Madagascar, a pink iguana in the Galápagos, a pancake tortoise in Tanzania,
see tangible benefits from conservation efforts.

Yet I can’t help but sense a perversity in all of this.

The initiative is being funded with Bezos’s blood money, as was his 2020
launch of the $10 billion greenwashed Earth Fund. All the cash Bezos is
throwing at the environment is nowhere near enough to offset the damage caused
by the creation of his obscene wealth, which places him in the top three
richest people on the planet. Amazon, the company that made him all that
money, is one of the world’s largest corporate climate polluters.
[![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Screen-
Shot-2026-08-13-at-10.50.37-AM.png)](https://www.pilsencommunitybooks.com/item/UfU8gx4LO98oZP-
hvrl3zQ)

Even under the company’s own accounting (which critics
[contend](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2024/sep/15/data-center-gas-
emissions-tech) is far from accurate), Amazon's 2025 carbon emissions
[surpassed](https://sustainability.aboutamazon.com/2025-report) its 2024
record, reaching 80 million metric tons, a 16% increase. Its electric
purchases, primarily for data centers,
[jumped](https://www.esgdive.com/news/amazon-2025-emissions-jump-as-ai-brings-
momentum-and-complexity-report/825667/) by 34%, and emissions from Amazon’s
fleet of delivery and transport vehicles increased by 20%, accounting for over
76% of its total carbon footprint.

This doesn’t even take into consideration the emissions from Bezos’s lavish
lifestyle and excessive investment portfolio. He owns two private jets and a
$500 million, 417-foot superyacht, which together emit about 10,000 tons of
CO2.

According to a damning Oxfam [report](https://www.oxfam.org/en/press-
releases/billionaires-emit-more-carbon-pollution-90-minutes-average-person-
does-lifetime), Bezos is responsible, through his corporations, investments
and consumption, for a [million times more carbon
pollution](https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2023/nov/20/twelve-
billionaires-climate-emissions-jeff-bezos-bill-gates-elon-musk-carbon-divide)
than the average person.

“The world’s poorest communities, those who have done the least to cause
climate change – those who are least able to respond and recover – are the
ones who are suffering the worst consequences. This is unfair and immoral,”
Oxfam International’s inequality policy adviser Alex Maitland
[told](https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2023/nov/20/twelve-
billionaires-climate-emissions-jeff-bezos-bill-gates-elon-musk-carbon-divide)
_The Guardian_.

Bezos’s contribution to climate change is about to get a whole lot worse.

A proposed data center in Pecos County, Texas, is so large that its 35 gas-
burning turbines, operating at 7.65 gigawatts, will make it the country's
single largest source of fossil fuel emissions. It will emit an insane [33
million tons of carbon
dioxide](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/08/climate/amazon-data-center-texas-
pollution.html) pollution each year.

“That’s a stunning amount of carbon exhaust, putting that single data center
in a league with [entire
countries](https://www.worldometers.info/co2-emissions/co2-emissions-by-
country/) including Switzerland, Ireland, and Bulgaria,”
[writes](https://futurism.com/artificial-intelligence/amazon-data-center-
largest-pollution-source-texas-usa) Joe Wilkins at _Futurism_.

This is just one more example (and I detail many more in the forthcoming [_Bad
Energy_](https://www.pilsencommunitybooks.com/item/iQd_fL9V8fi4CeCQDmhTjw)) of
why renewables can’t keep up with our ever-increasing demand for electricity,
thanks in no small part to billionaires like Jeff Bezos and Big Tech’s
appetite for data center destruction.

Amazon is relying on gas to run its fleet of servers because solar and wind
would require an immense amount of land to build out.

A solar farm requires up to [7,000 acres to supply 1
GW](https://seia.org/research-resources/land-use-and-solar-development/) of
electricity. For Amazon’s future data center in Texas (if we don’t stop it),
the company would need 49,000 acres of land covered with solar panels to
generate 7 GW of electricity. That’s over 76 square miles, roughly the size of
Madison, Wisconsin.

Sorry, Leo, I know you think you’re doing a good thing here by trying to save
imperiled species from extinction, but your buddy Jeff Bezos can’t buy his way
out of the destruction he’s manifested.

Oh, and while you're closing the door on Bezos, could you divest from that
[disgusting eco-resort](https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/articles/leonardo-
dicaprio-faces-backlash-co-104738961.html) you're helping finance in Israel,
too?

Thanks.
